scope: Official OpenHarmony 6.0 implementation and API 20 SDK reference inspected to interpret the benchmark. The tested image is OpenHarmony 6.1.0.31; this is source-based interpretation, not a runtime stack trace.
conclusion: AudioRenderer.write resolves with bytes written to the native stream, after queued asynchronous work. Native ring-buffer writes may wait for writable frames. Resolution is neither first speaker output nor proof that the entire recording has played.
measurement: The benchmark reports scheduler-decision to first accepted PCM write resolution. Dwell is separate. Emitted waveform capture is separate. Phase tracing records dispatch and resolution independently, plus actual buffer size and PCM duration.
compatibility: The write API is available since API 8 and deprecated since API 11 in favor of writeData callbacks. Deprecation does not make the recorded successful PCM writes a speaker-onset measurement.
